subject: maths
pattern: Vector Algebra gives 6-9 marks: 1-mark items on unit vectors or perpendicularity, 2/3-mark numericals on dot and cross products (projection, area, angle, perpendicular vector) and a 5-mark proof (sine rule, angle in a semicircle) or scalar triple product problem. Show the determinant for cross products clearly and always state the magnitude.

questions.q: Find the unit vector in the direction of $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k$.
questions.answer: $|\vec a|=\sqrt{4+9+1}=\sqrt{14}$. Unit vector $\hat a=\frac{\vec a}{|\vec a|}=\frac{2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k}{\sqrt{14}}$.

questions.q: If $\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a\times\vec b|$, find the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.
Find $\lambda$ if $\vec a=2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k$ are perpendicular.
Find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are $\vec a=3\hat i+\hat j+4\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$.
questions.answer: $\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\3&1&4\\1&-1&1\end{vmatrix}=5\hat i+\hat j-4\hat k$. Area $=|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{25+1+16}=\sqrt{42}$ square units.

questions.q: Find the angle between the vectors $\hat i+\hat j$ and $\hat j+\hat k$.
Find $\lambda$ for which the vectors $2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, $\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k$ and $3\hat i+\lambda\hat j+5\hat k$ are coplanar.
questions.answer: Coplanar if the scalar triple product is zero: $\begin{vmatrix}2&-1&1\\1&2&-3\\3&\lambda&5\end{vmatrix}=2(10+3\lambda)+1(5+9)+1(\lambda-6)=28+7\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-4$.

questions.q: Find a vector of magnitude 9 which is perpendicular to both $\vec a=4\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec b=-2\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k$.
questions.answer: $\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\4&-1&3\\-2&1&-2\end{vmatrix}=-\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k$, magnitude $\sqrt{1+4+4}=3$. Required vector $=\pm9\cdot\frac{-\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k}{3}=\pm(-3\hat i+6\hat j+6\hat k)$.

questions.q: Prove by vector method that the angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
questions.answer: Let $O$ be the centre, $AB$ a diameter with $\vec{OA}=\vec a$, $\vec{OB}=-\vec a$, and $P$ any point with $\vec{OP}=\vec p$, $|\vec p|=|\vec a|$. $\vec{PA}=\vec a-\vec p$, $\vec{PB}=-\vec a-\vec p$. $\vec{PA}\cdot\vec{PB}=-(\vec a-\vec p)\cdot(\vec a+\vec p)=-(|\vec a|^2-|\vec p|^2)=0$. Hence $PA\perp PB$, i.e. $\angle APB=90^\circ$.

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(1,1,2)$, $B(2,3,5)$, $C(1,5,5)$.
questions.answer: $\vec{AB}=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec{AC}=4\hat j+3\hat k$. $\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=-6\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k$. Area $=\frac12|\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}|=\frac12\sqrt{36+9+16}=\frac{\sqrt{61}}{2}$ square units.

questions.q: If $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=5$, $|\vec c|=7$, find the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.
questions.answer: $\vec c=-(\vec a+\vec b)\Rightarrow|\vec c|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2+2\vec a\cdot\vec b$. $49=9+25+30\cos\theta\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\frac12\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ$.

questions.q: Using vector method, prove the sine rule $\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{c}{\sin C}$ for a triangle $ABC$.
questions.answer: Let $\vec{BC}=\vec a$, $\vec{CA}=\vec b$, $\vec{AB}=\vec c$; then $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec0$. Cross with $\vec a$: $\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c\times\vec a$. Magnitudes: $ab\sin(\pi-C)=ca\sin(\pi-B)\Rightarrow b\sin C=c\sin B\Rightarrow\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}$. Cross with $\vec b$: $\vec b\times\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b$, giving $bc\sin A=ab\sin C\Rightarrow\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{c}{\sin C}$. Hence $\frac a{\sin A}=\frac b{\sin B}=\frac c{\sin C}$.

questions.q: Define scalar triple product. Show that $|\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)|$ is the volume of a parallelepiped and find the volume for $\vec a=2\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k$, $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$, $\vec c=3\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$.
questions.answer: Scalar triple product $[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$. $\vec b\times\vec c$ is perpendicular to the base with magnitude equal to the base area; height $=|\vec a|\cos\phi$, the projection of $\vec a$ on that normal. Volume $=$ base area $\times$ height $=|\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)|$. Here $\begin{vmatrix}2&-3&4\\1&2&-1\\3&-1&2\end{vmatrix}=2(4-1)+3(2+3)+4(-1-6)=6+15-28=-7$. Volume $=7$ cubic units.
